answers.q: publish-images.yml base image tags / ECR credentials / proof-os gates before push
answers.answer: The question's premise is partly wrong: there is no ECR anywhere in this repo. .github/workflows/publish-images.yml pushes to GHCR (ghcr.io/influoradigital-bit/influora-{api,ai,web}) using docker/login-action with username: ${{ github.actor }} and password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} (the built-in Actions token, not a stored PAT/IAM credential). Neither gate checks registry reachability/existence — there is no gate anywhere in .proof-os/ that blocks publication because a target registry 'does not yet exist'; GHCR always exists for a GitHub org, so that scenario as posed does not apply to this pipeline (it may have applied to an earlier design targeting a not-yet-provisioned VPS registry, but no such gate is present in this RC).

answers.q: Concurrent agents writing to .proof-os/ledger + SHARED_CONTEXT.md — race-condition prevention
answers.answer: Two distinct mechanisms exist, both partial: (1) .proof-os/gates/_lock.sh provides an atomic mkdir-based lock (gate_lock/gate_unlock) with a wait ceiling and stale-lock reaping by PID liveness, but this only serializes EXPENSIVE GATE LEGS (e.g. a shared npm-test run) between agents on one machine — it does not touch journal.jsonl/ledger/failures.jsonl writes or SHARED_CONTEXT.md edits at all. (2) For SHARED_CONTEXT.md and source-file collisions, the only control is a human/process convention: an 'ACTIVE ASSIGNMENTS' table assigns each owner a strictly non-overlapping set of file paths, plus the written rule 'Every owner re-reads their region after editing to confirm the change survived. No owner commits or pushes.' This is NOT a technical lock — it is discipline, and SHARED_CONTEXT.md itself documents that it has already failed ('this repo has a documented history of concurrent sessions clobbering in-progress edits'). No file locking, CRDT, or transactional merge for journal.jsonl/SHARED_CONTEXT.md was found anywhere in the RC.

No owner commits or pushes.' plus the ACTIVE ASSIGNMENTS ownership table; and .proof-os/gates/_lock.sh's gate_lock/gate_unlock mkdir-based lock with LOCK_WAITED/stale-reap logic.

answers.q: Meta token refresh mid-request: MetaTokenRefreshService async vs InstagramInsightsClient.getProfile() blocking
answers.answer: The premise that MetaTokenRefreshService 'runs async' is not supported by the code: it is a plain `@Scheduled(cron=...)` job with an in-process `AtomicBoolean running` overlap guard plus a `@SchedulerLock` (ShedLock) for cross-instance mutual exclusion — it is a synchronous, once-a-day batch sweep, not an `@Async` method. InstagramInsightsClient.getProfile() is confirmed blocking: it delegates to MetaGraphApiClient.get(), which uses Spring's synchronous `RestClient`. There is no retry-after-refresh logic inside MetaGraphApiClient.get() itself — a 401 from Meta is translated into a thrown `MetaTokenExpiredException` (translate() checks `status.value() == 401`), and the call simply fails; the caller must catch that exception and handle it (e.g. mark the token invalid), there is no automatic 'refresh then retry the same call' path visible in this client. So the actual gap is: if a token expires between the refresh sweep's daily check and a later insights call, that call fails with MetaTokenExpiredException and is not automatically retried after a fresh refresh within the same request.
answers.evidence: MetaTokenRefreshService.java: `@Scheduled(cron = "0 30 2 * * *") @SchedulerLock(...)` and `AtomicBoolean running` (no @Async anywhere in the class); InstagramInsightsClient.getProfile() -> apiClient.get(...) (synchronous RestClient); MetaGraphApiClient.java translate(): `if (status.value() == 401) { return new MetaTokenExpiredException(...); }` with no retry loop around the RestClient call.

answers.q: n8n trend-pull workflow crash mid-run — freshness guarantee, does a failed run block the next?
answers.answer: No cross-run interlock exists: n8n's `scheduleTrigger` nodes fire independently on their own cron schedule regardless of whether the previous run succeeded, failed, or is still executing (no code-level guard against overlapping runs was found in the workflow JSON). Within a single run, each HTTP/DB node has `retryOnFail: true, maxTries: 3` and the theme-tagger recovery call is fail-closed (any error -> drop that row, continue). The MySQL write step is a plain `operation: insert` (no ON DUPLICATE KEY / upsert), and cross-source dedup is done only in-memory for the current run via a `seen` Set keyed on `region|date|lower(text)` — there is no persisted dedup against ALREADY-INSERTED rows from a prior (possibly crashed) run, so a run that crashes AFTER inserting some rows but before completing, followed by the next scheduled run re-pulling the same day's sources, could insert duplicate trend rows for the same day (bounded only by the plain INSERT's own primary key, which is a fresh ULID per row, not a natural key — so duplicates would NOT be rejected by a DB constraint either). The workflow additionally ships with `"active": false`, so none of this runs on a schedule at all by default in this RC.
